See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Semester GPA = Σ(Course grade points × Course credits) ÷ Σ(GPA-bearing credits)

A worked example

A 3-credit course at 4.0 points contributes 12 quality points. A 4-credit course at 3.0 contributes 12, and a 2-credit course at 2.0 contributes 4. Total quality points are 28 across 9 credits: 28 ÷ 9 = 3.11, rounded to two decimal places.

Before you use the result

This calculator covers general course GPA and semester GPA on the same page because their arithmetic is identical. Selecting a maximum scale validates your numbers; it does not convert one grading system to another. Enter the points your school assigns to each course. Transfer courses, pass/fail grades and withdrawals may be excluded, and retake rules differ. A school that truncates GPA can report a slightly different number from this rounded planning estimate.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

Is this a US or Canadian GPA calculator?

It uses a credit-weighted formula with numeric grade points. You can select a compatible scale, but you must use your own institution’s conversion and inclusion rules.

Can I turn a percentage directly into a GPA?

There is no single correct conversion for every institution. Check the receiving institution’s grading table before entering grade points.

How do I combine semesters?

Use the cumulative GPA calculator with your previous GPA and credits plus the new semester GPA and credits. Avoid double-counting a semester.
